manifest.name: @mpd-dsh/mpd
manifest.description: A DeepSeek Harness plugin bundle: an eleven-role specialist roster, a durable workmate library, team staging with a shared board, and native dsh-Go panels and tool cards.

bundle.text:
# mpd-dsh bundle plugin layer (Plan D): ADDITIVE-ONLY, ZERO id-targets.
# (The two preset-selection registry id-targets this file used to carry were
# removed by the strict zero-override decision — see the two blocks below.)
# Policy: never id-target rows owned by the stock DSH templates (llm-deepseek /
# agent-default-model / skill-filesystem / llm-pi-ai) — id-target replaces the
# WHOLE stock config and would wipe the stock model list / provider defaults.
# DeepSeek official provider ships with dsh-base as-is; this bundle adds only:
# MCP servers, the mpd-* plugins, the OFFICIAL Agent Teams rows, and the
# agent-preset row that declares the `mpd` preset (the skill corpus is served by
# the mpd-bootstrap row's ctx.skills provider — nothing is copied into $DSH_HOME).
#
# ── HARNESS 0.1.7-rc.2: THE PRESET MODEL WAS REPLACED ───────────────────────
# `@deepseek-ai/dsh-agent-presets` — the directory/preset-root service this file
# used to id-target TWICE (the web plane row `agent-presets` and the dsh-tui plane
# row `dsh-tui-agent-presets`) — NO LONGER EXISTS in the installed harness. The
# role is split in two:
#   · `@deepseek-ai/dsh-agent-preset-registry` holds the deployment `default`;
#   · `@deepseek-ai/dsh-agent-preset` is ONE ROW PER PRESET, carrying that
#     preset's child entry list inline under `config.plugins`.
# The shipped presets follow exactly that shape: `@deepseek-ai/dsh-web-app`
# declares `presets/{standard,ptc,minimal,cordis}.patch.yml` and lists them as an
# ARRAY in its own `dsh.bundle.patch`. This bundle mirrors it: `package.json`'s
# `dsh.bundle.patch` is the array
#   [ "./cordis.patch.yml", "./presets/mpd.patch.yml" ]
# and the second file inserts the `preset-mpd` row. The retired directory form
# (`presets/mpd/{preset.yml,agent.cordis.yml}`) is gone; its content lives in
# `presets/mpd.patch.yml` verbatim, comments included.
#
# FILE-URL -> PATH (win32). `baseUrl` is a file URL and every path below is derived from it with
# plain string ops (a `!!js` expression has no imports). The win32 spelling is `file://` + `/` +
# `C:/...`, so stripping `file://` alone leaves `/C:/...` - which the OS reads as a path on the
# CURRENT drive and then composes into a doubled drive prefix, so every MCP row of the bundle dies
# with `Cannot find module` (measured 2026-09-22, bundle-lifecycle boot). The drive-letter
# lookahead drops the third slash for a drive path ONLY, which leaves the POSIX `/home/...` form
# byte-identical. `decodeURIComponent` is the other half: a URL percent-escapes what a path does
# not, and a Windows short name carries a tilde (`.../ZHAO%7E1.YIN/...`), so the raw form named a
# directory that does not exist (measured 2026-09-22, second boot).

# ── preset selection: the deployment default is HOST-OWNED and never id-targeted ──
# REMOVED (strict zero-override, user decision 2026-10-02). This block used to be
#   - id: agent-preset-registry
#     name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-agent-preset-registry'
#     config:
#       default: mpd
# and that id is declared by a HOST layer, not by us: `@deepseek-ai/dsh-web-app`'s
# OWN cordis.patch.yml declares id `agent-preset-registry` (name
# '@deepseek-ai/dsh-agent-preset-registry', config `{ default: standard }`). An
# id-target REPLACES a host layer's decision, which is exactly what this bundle's
# policy forbids — a shipped row may add a capability, never overwrite a host's.
# `node scripts/verify-no-host-override.ts` now fails the build on any future
# id-target whose id a host layer declares.
#
# WHY AN ADDITIVE SECOND REGISTRY ROW IS NOT THE WORKAROUND (the measured reason):
# two rows mounting the SAME package each call `reflect.provide('agentPresets', …)`,
# and a duplicate `provide` for one service name is a HARD cordis boot error — an
# extra registry row would take the whole boot down. There is no additive spelling
# of "change the deployment default".
#
# THE SUPPORTED CHANNEL IS THE USER'S OWN, and it is documented in
# `docs/preset-default.md` (bilingual pair; the exact steps and their trade-offs):
#   · web / headless -> the `selectedDefault` volatile field of the
#     `agent-preset-registry` entry, set from the Settings UI (the registry reads it
#     for new sessions and prefers it over the deployment `default`). This bundle
#     writes NOTHING itself.
#   · dsh-tui -> `/preset mpd` in the TUI, which persists
#     `{ "preset": "mpd" }` to `~/.dsh-tui/agent-preset.json`; or `DSH_TUI_PRESET=mpd`
#     in the user's OWN profile patch; or the one-command helper
#     `node scripts/set-default-preset.ts --yes` (dry-run by default), which writes
#     exactly that file through the sanctioned channel.
#
# CONSEQUENCE, stated so it is never a surprise: without that user action a profile
# falls back to the HOST default (`standard`), so `mpd` is OPT-IN after this
# removal, not the default. That regression is the price of the policy, and the doc
# plus the helper exist to make closing it one step.

# ── preset selection, dsh-tui plane: REMOVED for the same policy ────────────
# This block used to be
#   - id: dsh-tui-agent-preset-registry
#     name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-agent-preset-registry'
#     config:
#       default: mpd
# MEASURED against the installed `@deepseek-harness-tui/dsh-tui` (0.12.0; the
# reading below was RE-VERIFIED against 0.13.0 on 2026-10-06 by the
# `dsh-tui-013-adaptation` wave — the row id, its `{ default: standard }` config
# and its `presets/` contents are unchanged): the TUI
# mints its OWN registry row under the scoped id `dsh-tui-agent-preset-registry`
# (name '@deepseek-ai/dsh-agent-preset-registry', config `{ default: standard }`,
# disabled when an enabled `agent-preset-registry` entry already exists), declared
# by the TUI package's OWN cordis.patch.yml. That is a HOST layer again, so
# id-targeting it is the same forbidden override as the web-plane row above — and
# a dsh-tui profile composes no dsh-web-app layer, so the two rows never collide;
# each is skipped in the other's composition (`patch: entry <id> not found`).
#
# WHAT IT COST (the honest consequence): a dsh-tui profile now keeps the HOST
# default `standard`, and dsh-tui 0.12.0 ships no `standard` preset row (its
# `presets/` carries only `liangshen`), so a session that resolves the default
# fails to find it — the documented `agent-preset/not-found` — and composes without
# a preset. The user channel below closes that gap in one step; the failure is
# exactly why `docs/preset-default.md` exists.
#
# THE SUPPORTED CHANNEL IS THE USER'S OWN (see the block above for the shared
# reasoning and `docs/preset-default.md` for the steps):
#   · `/preset mpd` inside dsh-tui, which persists `{ "preset": "mpd" }` (written by
#     dsh-tui's own `writePresetPref`: `JSON.stringify({ preset }, null, 2)`, no
#     trailing newline) to `~/.dsh-tui/agent-preset.json`;
#   · `DSH_TUI_PRESET=mpd` in the user's own profile patch, which the TUI's
#     `config.preset` reads and which WINS over the persisted preference;
#   · `node scripts/set-default-preset.ts --yes` (dry-run by default), the
#     one-command helper that writes the same file through the same shape.
#
# SAFETY ARGUMENT RETIRED WITH IT: the old "each id exists in exactly ONE
# composition" argument was correct but is no longer load-bearing here, because
# this file now declares no id-target at all.

# ── runtime plugin dependency: the sidebar HOST the bundle's GUI needs ──────
# MEASURED DEFECT (evidence/install-deps/red-baseline/20260920T030832Z/result.json):
# a clean install of this bundle alone composed ZERO `dsh-better-sidebar` rows, so
# the `betterSidebar` service never existed and the bundle's two sidebar pages
# (mpd-agent-teams, mpd-workmate) registered nothing — the reported "the sidebar
# cannot display". The package is declared in the bundle manifest as an OPTIONAL PEER plus a
# devDependency (`dsh-better-sidebar 0.28.0`) — not as a `dependencies` entry — and MOUNTED here.
#
# BOTH halves are required. The declaration alone never mounts anything: `dsh plugin
# add` reconciles only PROFILE-level dependencies into `dsh.profile.bundles`, so a
# bundle's dependency never becomes a layer and the package's own guarded patch never
# applies. The row alone would be boot-fatal when the module is unresolvable
# (`assertEntriesLoaded`). What makes the row resolvable is
# `@deepseek-ai/dsh-app-boot#healProfileModuleFallback`, which materializes the
# dependency closure of every non-installation bundle layer into
# `<profile>/node_modules` before the loader runs (measured; see the ledger under
# evidence/install-deps/implementation/**).
#
# THE ENTRY ID IS DELIBERATELY `mpd-better-sidebar`, byte-different from the
# package's own patch id (`better-sidebar`) and from the aggregate's id
# (`web-ui-better-sidebar`, @linxin666/dsh-web-all): a duplicate loader ENTRY ID is
# fatal even when the guard would have disabled one of the two, so we never reuse an
# id another layer may mint.
#
# THE GUARD IS ORDER-INDEPENDENT — the property that makes BOTH install orders safe.
# `[...ctx.loader.entries()]` is FORWARD-BLIND at first evaluation (measured: the
# same expression re-evaluates later with every entry visible, but `Entry.refresh()`
# returns early once `this.fiber` exists, so the FIRST evaluation decides), and
# @linxin666/dsh-web-all mounts the sidebar with an UNGUARDED row. A guard that read
# only the entry list would kill a boot that works today whenever the aggregate is
# installed AFTER this bundle. So the guard reads DECLARATIONS instead:
#   1. no `dsh-better-sidebar` resolvable from `<profile>/node_modules` -> disable
#      (degrade to "no sidebar" with one warning, never fail the boot);
#   2. `dsh-better-sidebar` is itself a declared `dsh.profile.bundles` layer -> its
#      own patch mounts it -> disable;
#   3. every OTHER bundle layer's `dsh.bundle.patch` is scanned for a MOUNT (the row rule
#      below). Self-exclusion is by IDENTITY (the layer whose `package.json` name is
#      `@mpd-dsh/mpd` is SKIPPED), never by a substring of our own row id (review R4);
#   4. EVERY other patch layer the loader composes is scanned the same way (review R1):
#      `<profileDir>/cordis.patch.yml`, `$DSH_HOME/cordis.patch.yml`
#      (`<profileDir>/../../cordis.patch.yml`) and every `--patch` overlay path
#      recovered from `process.argv` (both `--patch X` and `--patch=X`, repeatable).
#      A sidebar row in any of them under a DIFFERENT entry id is exactly the
#      `duplicate prefix route` boot-killer (requirements F3) and is now seen;
#   5. no enabled `@deepseek-ai/dsh-host-webserver` ENTRY -> disable. The web-plane
#      clause is fail-closed (review R3): the raw `options.disabled` node must be
#      absent or literally `false`, so a webserver row disabled by an expression is NOT
#      "present", and the `@deepseek-ai/dsh-web-app` layer no longer enables this row on
#      its own — the service the sidebar injects is the entry's, not the layer's.
#
# THE ROW RULE (repair F1, stated verbatim — this IS the contract a reviewer tests):
#   1. Strip YAML comments before matching (a `#` that is not inside quotes ends the
#      line's content).
#   2. Find candidate ROWS that name `dsh-better-sidebar` (the `name:` value, quoted or
#      bare).
#   3. A candidate counts as a MOUNT unless it carries a LITERAL `disabled: true`.
#   4. Unknown / `!!js`-valued `disabled` counts as a MOUNT (conservative: we back off
#      rather than risk a duplicate).
#   5. Any parsing doubt falls back to the CURRENT behaviour (treat as a mount ->
#      DISABLED).
# The bias direction is unchanged and deliberate — a false disable costs the sidebar (one
# log line, the session keeps running); a false enable kills the whole boot with
# `webserver: duplicate route`. What changed with repair F1 is only HOW a candidate is
# recognised inside those files: a comment that mentions the package, or a foreign row
# that is literally `disabled: true`, mounts nothing and no longer suppresses our only
# mount (the verification lane measured both as a SILENT loss of the sidebar). When in
# doubt this guard disables.
# PROFILE-DIR DERIVATION (win32). Clause 1 needs the PROFILE DIRECTORY itself, and `baseUrl` is
# that directory's own file URL (`file:///C:/.../profiles/web/`), so it is converted with
# `node:url.fileURLToPath` — never with `new URL('.', baseUrl).pathname`. On win32 that
# `pathname` is `/C:/Users/<u>/.dsh/profiles/web/`, and win32 `path.normalize` reads its leading
# `/` as the CURRENT drive root, so the check tested `\C:\Users\...\node_modules\dsh-better-sidebar`:
# `fs.existsSync` answered false for a sidebar that WAS resolvable, and clause 1 disabled this row
# on EVERY win32 profile with the reason above, which reads as "not installed" while the package
# sits in the profile (measured 2026-09-23, win32-x64 / node v24.21.0, both red and green under
# evidence/install-deps/sidebar-guard-win32/). That is the same doubled-drive-prefix class the
# FILE-URL header at the top of this file fixes for the path rows; `fileURLToPath` is used here
# rather than that string-op idiom because this scalar is YAML DOUBLE-quoted (the idiom's `\/`
# would need escaping there) and because a real path is what `fs` is handed.
# The whole guard is one try/catch that returns TRUE (disabled) on ANY throw, so the
# worst case is a missing sidebar, never a dead boot. It appends ONE line per distinct
# decision with the stable prefix `[mpd-better-sidebar] mount guard: ` to the log FILE
# `<root>/.mpd/logs/mpd-patch-guards.log` — R5: a guard line never goes to the terminal,
# and `logGuard` mirrors `packages/mpd-mcp-shared/log-sink.ts`'s root chain EXACTLY
# (MPD_MCP_LOG_DIR -> DSH_WORKSPACE_ROOT -> cwd -> os.tmpdir), because a `!!js` expression
# has no imports and that module stays the SINGLE owner of the semantics. Raw `e.options.disabled` is read
# on purpose: reading another entry's EVALUATED `disabled` getter re-enters its own
# `!!js` expression (measured: mutual recursion, stack overflow).
- insert:
    - id: mpd-better-sidebar
      # A file:// URL as the row name MOUNTS (measured) but does NOT survive the loader's PEER
      # VALIDATION: the row is then disabled with `its declared peer dependencies cannot be
      # validated: name.startsWith is not a function`, because the validator is handed a URL where it
      # expects a package name. So the name stays the bare specifier, and the bundle's own copy is
      # reached through `mpd-better-sidebar-host` instead (see that package: it re-exports the host by
      # a RELATIVE path, so the host's package.json is never loaded as a row and never validated).
      # REACHED THROUGH THE BUNDLE'S OWN NAME, which is the ONE specifier that resolves on BOTH
      # installs: a packed install resolves it through its own package, and a checkout install
      # through the linked bundle (`@mpd-dsh/mpd/node_modules/...` IS the file the bundle ships).
      # The bare specifier `dsh-better-sidebar` resolves only when the PROFILE's node_modules has it,
      # which `healProfileModuleFallback` does not produce for a `link:` layer (measured), and a
      # file:// URL as the row name mounts but then fails the loader's PEER VALIDATION with
      # `name.startsWith is not a function` (measured).
      name: '@mpd-dsh/mpd/packages/mpd-better-sidebar-host/dist/index.js'
      disabled: !!js "(() => { const logGuard = (text) => { try { const gfs = process.getBuiltinModule('node:fs'); const gpath = process.getBuiltinModule('node:path'); const gos = process.getBuiltinModule('node:os'); let cwd = ''; try { cwd = process.cwd() } catch (e) {} const roots = [process.env.MPD_MCP_LOG_DIR, process.env.DSH_WORKSPACE_ROOT, cwd, gos.tmpdir()]; for (const root of roots) { if (typeof root !== 'string' || root.trim() === '') { continue } try { const dir = gpath.join(root, '.mpd', 'logs'); gfs.mkdirSync(dir, { recursive: true }); gfs.appendFileSync(gpath.join(dir, 'mpd-patch-guards.log'), text + String.fromCharCode(10)); return } catch (e) {} } } catch (e) {} }; const say = (decision, reason) => { try { const seen = globalThis.__mpdSidebarGuardSeen || (globalThis.__mpdSidebarGuardSeen = {}); const key = decision + '|' + reason; if (!seen[key]) { seen[key] = 1; logGuard('[mpd-better-sidebar] mount guard: ' + decision + ' - ' + reason) } } catch (e) {} }; try { const fs = process.getBuiltinModule('node:fs'); const path = process.getBuiltinModule('node:path'); const profileDir = path.normalize(process.getBuiltinModule('node:url').fileURLToPath(baseUrl)); const readJson = (p) => { try { return JSON.parse(fs.readFileSync(p, 'utf8')) } catch (e) { return null } }; const readText = (p) => { try { return fs.readFileSync(p, 'utf8') } catch (e) { return null } }; const SQ = String.fromCharCode(39); const DQ = String.fromCharCode(34); const HASH = String.fromCharCode(35); const LF = String.fromCharCode(10); const TAB = String.fromCharCode(9); const stripComments = (text) => { const out = []; for (const line of String(text).split(LF)) { let kept = ''; let quote = ''; for (const ch of line) { if (quote === '') { if (ch === HASH) { break } if (ch === SQ || ch === DQ) { quote = ch } } else if (ch === quote) { quote = '' } kept += ch } out.push(kept) } return out.join(LF) }; const unquote = (raw) => { const t = String(raw).trim(); if (t.length > 1 && (t.charAt(0) === SQ || t.charAt(0) === DQ) && t.charAt(t.length - 1) === t.charAt(0)) { return t.slice(1, -1) } return t }; const indentOf = (line) => { let i = 0; while (i < line.length && (line.charAt(i) === ' ' || line.charAt(i) === TAB)) { i++ } return i }; const keyOf = (line, key) => { let t = line; if (t.charAt(0) === '-' && t.charAt(1) === ' ') { t = t.slice(2) } const trimmed = t.trimStart(); if (!trimmed.startsWith(key + ':')) { return null } return trimmed.slice(key.length + 1).trim() }; const foreignRowMountsSidebar = (text) => { const stripped = stripComments(text); if (stripped.indexOf('dsh-better-sidebar') < 0) { return false } const rows = []; let current = null; for (const line of stripped.split(LF)) { if (line.trim() === '') { continue } const indent = indentOf(line); const body = line.slice(indent); const isItem = body.charAt(0) === '-' && (body.length === 1 || body.charAt(1) === ' '); if (isItem) { current = { indent, lines: [] }; rows.push(current) } if (current !== null && (isItem || indent > current.indent)) { current.lines.push({ indent, body }) } } let named = false; let mounting = false; for (const row of rows) { let nameValue = null; let nameIndent = -1; let disabledValue = null; let disabledIndent = -1; for (const entry of row.lines) { const nv = keyOf(entry.body, 'name'); if (nv !== null && (nameIndent < 0 || entry.indent < nameIndent)) { nameIndent = entry.indent; nameValue = nv } const dv = keyOf(entry.body, 'disabled'); if (dv !== null && (disabledIndent < 0 || entry.indent < disabledIndent)) { disabledIndent = entry.indent; disabledValue = dv } } if (nameValue === null || unquote(nameValue) !== 'dsh-better-sidebar') { continue } named = true; const literallyDisabled = disabledValue !== null && disabledIndent <= nameIndent && unquote(disabledValue).toLowerCase() === 'true'; if (!literallyDisabled) { mounting = true } } if (mounting) { return true } if (!named) { return true } return false }; const ownModules = path.join(profileDir, 'node_modules'); const hostDirs = [path.join(ownModules, 'dsh-better-sidebar'), path.join(ownModules, '@mpd-dsh', 'mpd', 'node_modules', 'dsh-better-sidebar')]; if (!hostDirs.some((dir) => fs.existsSync(dir))) { say('DISABLED', 'dsh-better-sidebar is resolvable from neither the profile node_modules nor the bundle'); return true } const manifest = readJson(path.join(profileDir, 'package.json')); const bundles = manifest && manifest.dsh && manifest.dsh.profile && Array.isArray(manifest.dsh.profile.bundles) ? manifest.dsh.profile.bundles : []; if (bundles.indexOf('dsh-better-sidebar') >= 0) { say('DISABLED', 'dsh-better-sidebar is itself a declared bundle layer'); return true } for (const bundle of bundles) { const name = String(bundle); for (const dir of [path.join(ownModules, name), path.join(profileDir, '..', 'node_modules', name)]) { const other = readJson(path.join(dir, 'package.json')); if (!other) continue; if (other.name === '@mpd-dsh/mpd') continue; const rel = other.dsh && other.dsh.bundle ? other.dsh.bundle.patch : undefined; if (typeof rel !== 'string') continue; const text = readText(path.join(dir, rel)); if (text !== null && foreignRowMountsSidebar(text)) { say('DISABLED', 'bundle layer ' + name + ' already mounts it in its own patch'); return true } } } const argv = Array.isArray(process.argv) ? process.argv : []; const overlays = []; for (let i = 0; i < argv.length; i++) { const arg = typeof argv[i] === 'string' ? argv[i] : ''; if (arg === '--patch' && typeof argv[i + 1] === 'string') { overlays.push(argv[i + 1]) } else if (arg.indexOf('--patch=') === 0) { overlays.push(arg.slice(8)) } } const layers = [path.join(profileDir, 'cordis.patch.yml'), path.join(profileDir, '..', '..', 'cordis.patch.yml')]; if (typeof process.env.DSH_HOME === 'string' && process.env.DSH_HOME !== '') { layers.push(path.join(process.env.DSH_HOME, 'cordis.patch.yml')) } for (const overlay of overlays) { layers.push(path.resolve(overlay)) } for (const layer of layers) { const text = readText(layer); if (text !== null && foreignRowMountsSidebar(text)) { say('DISABLED', 'patch layer ' + layer + ' already mounts it'); return true } } const entries = [...ctx.loader.entries()]; const hasWebEntry = entries.some((e) => e.options && e.options.name === '@deepseek-ai/dsh-host-webserver' && (e.options.disabled === undefined || e.options.disabled === false)); if (!hasWebEntry) { say('DISABLED', 'no enabled @deepseek-ai/dsh-host-webserver entry in this composition'); return true } say('ENABLED', 'web plane present and no other layer mounts dsh-better-sidebar'); return false } catch (e) { try { logGuard('[mpd-better-sidebar] mount guard: DISABLED - guard threw ' + String(e && e.message ? e.message : e)) } catch (e2) {} return true } })()"

- insert:
    # B8 (wave 2): this row names NO binary path any more. It launches
    # packages/mpd-mcp-astgrep/dist/launch.js, which resolves the binary
    # bundle-relatively (env pin -> $MPD_AST_GREP_BIN_DIR -> createRequire of the
    # optionalDependency -> <bundle>/.toolchain/node_modules/.bin/ast-grep|sg) and
    # sets MPD_AST_GREP_SG_PATH only when the caller left it unset, before the
    # adopted server reads it. The old `env.MPD_AST_GREP_SG_PATH = <baseUrl>/node_modules/.bin/sg`
    # pin was packed-layout-only AND named the deprecated `sg` wrapper (exit 1);
    # a mounting boot with no env pin is the gate (never `--dump-config`).
    - id: mcp-astgrep
      name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-mcp-client'
      config:
        serverName: ast_grep
        transport: stdio
        command: node
        args:
          - !!js 'process.env.MPD_DSH_ASTGREP_CLI || ((typeof baseUrl === "string" ? decodeURIComponent(baseUrl.replace(/^file:\/\/\/(?=[A-Za-z]:)/, "").replace(/^file:\/\//, "")).replace(/\/+$/, "") : "") + "/node_modules/@mpd-dsh/mpd/packages/mpd-mcp-astgrep/dist/launch.js")'
        toolCallTimeoutMs: 60000
    # ONE old row became TWO (de-omo wave B2). `mcp-gitbash` started one vendored server whose
    # tools were a raw shell runner (`run`, `which_bash`, `diagnose`) — not a git toolbox. The capability
    # is now re-sourced from two DECLARED npm dependencies, and one MCP client row starts exactly one
    # server process, so the row split follows the packages: `mcp-git` (the git toolbox) and `mcp-shell`
    # (the raw shell runner that replaces the old tools). Both rows ship `disabled: true`, the posture
    # the single old row already had; enable the one you want with `disabled: false`.
    - id: mcp-git
      name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-mcp-client'
      disabled: true
      config:
        serverName: git
        transport: stdio
        command: node
        args:
          - !!js 'process.env.MPD_DSH_GIT_CLI || ((typeof baseUrl === "string" ? decodeURIComponent(baseUrl.replace(/^file:\/\/\/(?=[A-Za-z]:)/, "").replace(/^file:\/\//, "")).replace(/\/+$/, "") : "") + "/node_modules/@mpd-dsh/mpd/packages/mpd-mcp-gitbash/dist/launch.js")'
          - git
        toolCallTimeoutMs: 60000
    - id: mcp-shell
      name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-mcp-client'
      disabled: true
      config:
        serverName: shell
        transport: stdio
        command: node
        args:
          - !!js 'process.env.MPD_DSH_SHELL_CLI || ((typeof baseUrl === "string" ? decodeURIComponent(baseUrl.replace(/^file:\/\/\/(?=[A-Za-z]:)/, "").replace(/^file:\/\//, "")).replace(/\/+$/, "") : "") + "/node_modules/@mpd-dsh/mpd/packages/mpd-mcp-gitbash/dist/launch.js")'
          - shell
        toolCallTimeoutMs: 60000
    # The `mcp-lsp` row is unchanged in SHAPE, and its SERVER is new: the vendored lsp-daemon
    # was replaced by the declared npm dependency `cclsp` (MIT), resolved by the launcher from the
    # installed profile. cclsp takes no subcommand, so the old literal `mcp` argv entry is gone. The
    # published tool names therefore follow cclsp's own 12 tools (mcp__lsp__find_definition,

# ── OFFICIAL Agent Teams rows (harness 0.1.7-rc.2) ──────────────────────────
# The bundle's team capability is the OFFICIAL plugin set, not a vendored body:
#   @deepseek-ai/dsh-experimental-agent-team          -> ctx.agentTeams (TeamService:
#       implicit-root roster, durable peer mailbox, shared task DAG)
#   @deepseek-ai/dsh-experimental-tool-agent-team     -> the scoped model-facing tools.
#       The team-door guard REFUSES the five authoring verbs (`spawn_teammate`,
#       `team_task_create|list|get|update`), so the team door is `agent_teams_plan`
#       (stage -> add_member / create_task, each task carrying its dependency answer
#       `blocked_by` or `independent: true`, -> approve) and the board is
#       `agent_teams_task` / `agent_teams_dispatch`; `send_message` / `list_agents` /
#       `wait_agent` / `interrupt_agent` stay for agent communication, plus the
#       `team:policy` prompt section
#   @deepseek-ai/dsh-experimental-client-ui-agent-team -> the Web roster, task board
#       and teammate navigation
# All three are declared in this package's `dependencies`, so
# `@deepseek-ai/dsh-app-boot#healProfileModuleFallback` materializes them into
# `<profile>/node_modules` before the loader runs and the rows always resolve (the
# `dsh-better-sidebar` pattern: the declaration alone mounts nothing, and a row
# alone would be boot-fatal when the module is unresolvable).
#
# ENTRY IDS ARE mpd-OWNED ON PURPOSE. `@deepseek-ai/dsh-experimental-agent-team-profile`
# mounts the same three packages under the ids `agent-team` / `tool-agent-team` /
# `ui-agent-team`, and a duplicate loader entry id is FATAL even when one side is
# disabled. mpd-prefixed ids keep the two layers installable side by side.
#
# `freshProvider`/`forkProvider` are the harness defaults (`spawn` / `fork`) and
# the official defaults. They are restated so a reader sees the resolution: the
# official TeamService forwards ONLY `{ prompt, parent }` to
# `ctx.subagents.startContinuable`, so a subagent provider cannot inject a
# per-teammate model route, persona or tool filter for a continuable teammate.
# That reduction is recorded in `docs/plan-0.1.7-adaptation.md` §3; the roster's
# per-agent `agentRoutes` routes survive on the one-shot consult path, and its read-only discipline
# is re-implemented as a tool guard by mpd-roles.
#
# The official profile bundle ALSO disables `tool-subagent`,
# `tool-subagent-control`, `tool-subagent-list-agents` and `tool-subagent-fork`.
# This bundle deliberately does NOT: the mpd preset mounts direct delegation as
# well, exactly as it did before, so a session keeps both the one-shot `subagent`
# path and the durable team path.
#
# ── TUI PLANE: THE OFFICIAL TEAM SERVICE ROWS ARE DISABLED IN A dsh-tui
#    COMPOSITION (the `disabled` guard on the two rows below) ────────────────
# MEASURED (2026-09-29, TUI profile, harness 0.2.0-rc.1 + dsh-tui 0.11.2,
# evidence/tui/team-plane-not-mountable/): with the bundle installed into a
# `dsh-tui` profile the team service row FAILS TO ACTIVATE —
#   `mpd-agent-team (@deepseek-ai/dsh-experimental-agent-team): Error:
#    dsh-tui: root.effect is unavailable from a plugin activation`
# — and `mpd-tool-agent-team` then reports `pending (waiting for service:
# agentTeams)` for the rest of the run.
#
# WHY IT CANNOT BE FIXED FROM THIS PATCH. `TeamService`'s constructor ends with
# `ctx.effect(() => { const dispose = ctx.root.sessionProjections.register(...) })`
# (`@deepseek-ai/dsh-experimental-agent-team` lib/index.js, `TeamService`): the
# projection is reached through `ctx.root`, and Cordis binds a service call to
# the CALLER's context, so `register()` runs with the ROOT context and its
# `this.ctx.effect(...)` creates an effect on the ROOT FIBER. The dsh-tui host
# wraps exactly that capability and refuses it from any plugin activation:
# `lib/types/dsh-adapter/host-access.js` rejects `root.effect` when the ambient
# activation is not the composition root, and the reason is written down in
# `host-access.d.ts`: "A plugin can read `ctx.root`, but using its root-bound
# service proxy would attach cleanup to the host fiber and leave the effect
# alive after the plugin unloads." The refusal is a property of the HOST, not
# of any row value — the plugin's own `Config` has no projection toggle, the
# call is unconditional, and it throws before any registration/dedup logic — so
# no `config`, no mount order and no isolation realm can make that activation
# succeed. Both `ctx.root`-bound call sites are identical in the 0.1.7-rc.2 copy
# this bundle pins and in the 0.2.0-rc.1 copy the harness ships, so pinning
# either version changes nothing.
#
# WHAT THIS PATCH DOES: the two rows that exist ONLY to serve that service are
# disabled in a composition that mounts the dsh-tui host — `mpd-agent-team`
# (the service itself; the row that throws) and `mpd-tool-agent-team` (its
# model-facing tools, which would otherwise wait for a service that can never
# arrive). `mpd-ui-agent-team` stays mounted: it is a Web CLIENT contribution
# (docs/tui.md NOT-CLAIMED #3), it registers nothing the TUI renders and it
# breaks nothing — disabling it would be a change beyond this defect.
#
# ── W5 OF THE TEAM-PLANE SPLIT: WHY THIS GUARD IS **KEPT** (2026-09-30) ────
# The split removed the REASON THE TEAM NEEDED THAT ROW and did NOT remove the
# reason the ROW cannot mount. Stated separately, because conflating them is how
# a guard gets deleted as "no longer needed" and a boot error comes back:
#
#   * WHAT THE SPLIT FIXED. The mpd team is now its own record
#     (`mpd-team-core-plugin`, `.mpd/team/teams/<id>.json`, served as
#     `mpdTeams`) and its own EXECUTOR (`mpd-dsh-adapter`'s `TeamExecutor`,
#     native by default over `ctx.subagents.startContinuable`, which needs
#     NOTHING from the official plugin). A dsh-tui composition therefore has a
#     WORKING team plane with these two rows disabled — W2's boot line says so
#     in as many words: `team executor: native (native: the default backend —
#     it needs nothing from the official plugin)`, and the W3 scene renders the
#     record's own dependency graph.
#   * WHAT IT CANNOT FIX, and this is the whole of the remaining argument:
#     `TeamService`'s ROOT-bound `sessionProjections.register` above. It is a
#     property of the dsh-tui HOST's capability wrapper, not of any row value,
#     not of the pinned version, and not of anything this bundle owns. Enabling
#     `mpd-agent-team` in a TUI composition does not give the TUI plane a team
#     service — it gives it the SAME activation error on every boot, which is
#     the defect this guard was added for.
#
# So the guard's justification is RE-SCOPED, not preserved by inertia: it no
# longer says "the team plane would be dead here" (untrue since W2) and it says
# "a row that cannot mount in this composition would print an activation error
# on every boot, and disabling it costs the TUI plane nothing" (true, and now
# measurable — the team works either way).
#
# WHAT IS LEFT IN A TUI PLANE (stated so no reader assumes more): the mpd team
# WORKFLOW rows stay mounted by design — `agent_teams_plan`/`_task`/`_mail`/
# `_control` keep their file-backed actions (`<workspace>/.mpd/team/`) and read
# the official roster defensively, so they degrade per action instead of
# vanishing; and since W2 the actions that used to fail (approve, dispatch, a
# teammate message) go through the NATIVE executor and work. The Web/headless
# plane is untouched: the guard returns false unless a dsh-tui host row is
# actually composed.
#
# THE GUARD RULE (identical shape to the `mpd-better-sidebar` mount guard — a
# `!!js` row-metadata expression evaluated against the Loader context at every
# mount decision, order-independent because it reads only DECLARATIONS already
# composed): disable when any composed entry IS the dsh-tui host — its `name` is
# `@deepseek-harness-tui/dsh-tui` or one of its subpaths, or its `id` starts
# with `dsh-tui`. A guard that throws keeps the row ENABLED and appends one line to
# `<root>/.mpd/logs/mpd-patch-guards.log` (R5 — never the terminal): a false disable
# would silently remove the team plane from a working Web profile, which is worse than
# the loud TUI error this fixes.

      disabled: !!js "(() => { const logGuard = (text) => { try { const gfs = process.getBuiltinModule('node:fs'); const gpath = process.getBuiltinModule('node:path'); const gos = process.getBuiltinModule('node:os'); let cwd = ''; try { cwd = process.cwd() } catch (e) {} const roots = [process.env.MPD_MCP_LOG_DIR, process.env.DSH_WORKSPACE_ROOT, cwd, gos.tmpdir()]; for (const root of roots) { if (typeof root !== 'string' || root.trim() === '') { continue } try { const dir = gpath.join(root, '.mpd', 'logs'); gfs.mkdirSync(dir, { recursive: true }); gfs.appendFileSync(gpath.join(dir, 'mpd-patch-guards.log'), text + String.fromCharCode(10)); return } catch (e) {} } } catch (e) {} }; try { const hit = [...ctx.loader.entries()].some((e) => { const o = e && e.options; if (!o) return false; const n = typeof o.name === 'string' ? o.name : ''; const i = typeof o.id === 'string' ? o.id : ''; return n.indexOf('@deepseek-harness-tui/dsh-tui') === 0 || i.indexOf('dsh-tui') === 0 }); if (!hit) return false; try { const seen = globalThis.__mpdTuiPlaneGuard || (globalThis.__mpdTuiPlaneGuard = {}); if (seen.said !== true) { seen.said = true; logGuard('[mpd-agent-team] DISABLED in a dsh-tui composition: the official team plugin registers its session projection through a ROOT-bound sessionProjections proxy, and the dsh-tui host refuses root.effect from a plugin activation - mpd-agent-team and mpd-tool-agent-team stay unmounted. THE MPD TEAM IS UNAFFECTED: since the team-plane split (W2) it runs on the NATIVE executor over ctx.subagents, which needs nothing from this row (see cordis.patch.yml TUI PLANE / W5)') } } catch (e) {} return true } catch (e) { try { logGuard('[mpd-agent-team] TUI-plane guard threw (' + String(e && e.message ? e.message : e) + ') - the row stays ENABLED; re-check the guard in cordis.patch.yml') } catch (e2) {} return false } })()"
      config:
        maxMembers: 16
        maxTasks: 256
        maxMessageBytes: 32768
        disposalTimeoutMs: 5000

      disabled: !!js "(() => { const logGuard = (text) => { try { const gfs = process.getBuiltinModule('node:fs'); const gpath = process.getBuiltinModule('node:path'); const gos = process.getBuiltinModule('node:os'); let cwd = ''; try { cwd = process.cwd() } catch (e) {} const roots = [process.env.MPD_MCP_LOG_DIR, process.env.DSH_WORKSPACE_ROOT, cwd, gos.tmpdir()]; for (const root of roots) { if (typeof root !== 'string' || root.trim() === '') { continue } try { const dir = gpath.join(root, '.mpd', 'logs'); gfs.mkdirSync(dir, { recursive: true }); gfs.appendFileSync(gpath.join(dir, 'mpd-patch-guards.log'), text + String.fromCharCode(10)); return } catch (e) {} } } catch (e) {} }; try { const hit = [...ctx.loader.entries()].some((e) => { const o = e && e.options; if (!o) return false; const n = typeof o.name === 'string' ? o.name : ''; const i = typeof o.id === 'string' ? o.id : ''; return n.indexOf('@deepseek-harness-tui/dsh-tui') === 0 || i.indexOf('dsh-tui') === 0 }); if (!hit) return false; try { const seen = globalThis.__mpdTuiPlaneGuard || (globalThis.__mpdTuiPlaneGuard = {}); if (seen.said !== true) { seen.said = true; logGuard('[mpd-agent-team] DISABLED in a dsh-tui composition: the official team plugin registers its session projection through a ROOT-bound sessionProjections proxy, and the dsh-tui host refuses root.effect from a plugin activation - mpd-agent-team and mpd-tool-agent-team stay unmounted (see cordis.patch.yml TUI PLANE)') } } catch (e) {} return true } catch (e) { try { logGuard('[mpd-agent-team] TUI-plane guard threw (' + String(e && e.message ? e.message : e) + ') - the row stays ENABLED; re-check the guard in cordis.patch.yml') } catch (e2) {} return false } })()"

# The `mpd` agent preset, as a 0.1.7-rc.2 PRESET ROW.
#
# HARNESS MODEL CHANGE (measured against @deepseek-ai/dsh@0.1.7-rc.2): presets are
# no longer directories served by `@deepseek-ai/dsh-agent-presets` (that package
# was REMOVED). The registry (@deepseek-ai/dsh-agent-preset-registry) holds only
# the `default` selection; every preset is an ordinary plugin row —
# `@deepseek-ai/dsh-agent-preset` with `config.id` plus the inline child plugin
# list below. This file is that row, and it is the bundle's ONLY declaration of
# the mpd composition: `package.json` lists it as the second entry of
# `dsh.bundle.patch`, after the main bundle patch. That main patch used to
# id-target `agent-preset-registry` to `default: mpd`; since the strict
# zero-override decision (2026-10-02) it does NOT — this bundle ships its preset
# ADDITIVELY and the deployment default stays the HOST's, so making `mpd` the
# default is a USER action (`/preset mpd` -> ~/.dsh-tui/agent-preset.json,
# `DSH_TUI_PRESET=mpd`, the Web Settings `selectedDefault`, or
# `node scripts/set-default-preset.ts --yes`). See docs/preset-default.md and the
# gate `scripts/verify-no-host-override.ts`.
#
# The child list is the former `presets/mpd/agent.cordis.yml`, moved here
# verbatim (comments included) because a patch layer has no `include:` — the
# loader's patch files are plain entry lists, and `applyEntryPatches` reads only
# `id` / `insert` / `name` plus per-key overrides.
#
# ONE row changed with the move: `workflow-worker-thread`
# (`@deepseek-ai/dsh-workflow-worker-thread`) no longer exists in the installed
# harness; the shipped `standard` preset declares `workflow-ptc`
# (`@deepseek-ai/dsh-workflow-ptc`, `provider: spawn`) instead, so this preset
# now matches it. Measured by resolving every `name:` in this file against
# `<dsh>/node_modules/@deepseek-ai/`.

- insert:
    - id: preset-mpd
      name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-agent-preset'
      config:
        id: mpd
        order: 1
        name: "MPD (Main Working Agent)"
        description: "The my-power-dsh main agent: reads AGENT.md/AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md for every project, works natively, consults the specialists in single calls (Architect/Researcher/Planner/Deep Worker/Senior Engineer/Lead/Explorer/Reviewer/Plan Reviewer/Vision Analyst/Junior Engineer) via mpd_role_spawn, and runs teams through the official @deepseek-ai/dsh-experimental-agent-team plugin."
        plugins:
          # The `mpd` agent preset: the bundle's main working agent (derived from the
          # shipped `standard` preset). Conventions carried by this preset:
          #  1) AGENT.md / AGENTS.md / CLAUDE.md workspace instructions are discovered and
          #     injected for every project session (see the agent-instructions row below);
          #  2) tool presentation is native (every row tool exposed directly to the model);
          #  3) the specialist roster's 11 specialists are NOT presets: they are specialist
          #     subagents (mpd-roles-plugin, mpd_role_spawn) and teammate instantiation
          #     templates for the OFFICIAL Agent Teams plugin (staged through
          #     `agent_teams_plan`; the captain takes a member's persona text from
          #     mpd_role_persona, and the roster is also
          #     served as an agent-scoped prompt section by mpd-roles-plugin);
          #  4) ROW SET = the shipped `standard` preset's. The harness moves capabilities
          #     between the host plane and the preset plane between releases (the Web
          #     overlay disables the host `tool-goal`/`command-goal` rows, and `present`
          #     only exists from 0.1.5-alpha.2 on), so this preset is kept row-for-row in
          #     step with `standard` — a missing row is a missing capability for every mpd
          #     session. `skills/dsh-qa/scripts/preset-conformance.ts` checks both the
          #     row set and every row config against the INSTALLED harness at gate time.
          #
          # This file is an AGENT-PLANE composition. The roster mounts it ONCE under a
          # standing scope; every session naming it joins by scope parentage, so the
          # tools and prompt sections registered here cover each joined agent while a
          # session's own state stays keyed per Session/Agent inside the plugins. The
          # host composition (`base.cordis.yml` + `web.cordis.yml`) keeps everything a
          # preset must not own: the registries themselves, the sandbox and approval
          # stack, persistence, and the model route.
          #
          # A service row here MUST sit inside a group carrying an `isolate` realm.
          # Without one it publishes into the root realm, where it is process-global —
          # another preset publishing the same name collides, and a host reader would
          # resolve one preset's instance for every session; `dsh-agent-presets` rejects
          # that at mount. `true` means an entry-local realm: this standing mount's own
          # private instance, apart from every other preset's. (A shared label does NOT
          # pool instances — `provide()` throws on the second registration under the
          # same realm symbol; labels join REALMS, and are not what this file needs.)

          # ── identity ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

          # The preset's own persona, shadowing the deployment default for this agent.
          # `{{model}}` is the ONLY prompt variable safe here: the loop registers `provider`
          # and `model`, and DELIBERATELY does not register `{{cwd}}` — an unresolved
          # reference throws during prompt assembly, before any model request (the
          # dsh-system-prompt README, 0.2.1-rc.5, says so explicitly). The
          # working-directory service supplies the current directory as literal runtime
          # context, so the persona must not restate it with a template variable.
          #
          # HARNESS CONTRACT: `dsh-persona` takes `prefix` (+ optional `suffix`), NOT the
          # single `text` key this row used through harness 0.1.2-rc.1 — that generation
          # registered one persona section. From 0.1.3-alpha.2 on the row is split into
          # the deployment persona prefix/suffix sections and `prefix` is REQUIRED, so a
          # `text:` row does not merely lose its persona: the config fails validation and
          # `dsh-agent-presets` refuses to mount THIS WHOLE PRESET (`agent-preset/invalid:
          # failed to apply loader entry persona … $.prefix missing required value`), i.e.
          # every mpd session fails to start. The long persona text therefore lives in
          # `prefix` and `suffix` keeps its empty default.
          - id: persona
            name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-persona'
            config:
              prefix: >-
                You are MPD, the main working agent of the my-power-dsh DeepSeek Harness bundle,
                powered by the {{model}} model.

                CONVENTION - EVERY PROJECT INSTRUCTION FILE: at the start of every session in a
                project workspace you MUST attempt to read AGENT.md (fall back to AGENTS.md, then
                CLAUDE.md) from the project root down to the current directory, and follow it. Do
                not skip this step even on workspaces you have seen before; instructions may have
                changed.

                READ DISCIPLINE — THE FIRST RULE OF EVERY TOP-LEVEL MPD SESSION (the captain; a delegated member reads the sources it was sent to read), decided BEFORE your first tool call. Reconnaissance is DELEGATED, never attempted:
                  * STEP 0, CLASSIFY THE TARGET. The DOCUMENTATION BAND is yours to read directly: `.mpd/**`, `docs/**`, `evidence/**`, `agent-references/**`, and the root `AGENT.md` / `AGENTS.md` / `CLAUDE.md` / `README*.md` / `CHANGELOG.md` / `LICENSE*.md`. Anything else — `src/**`, `packages/**`, `scripts/**`, `tests/**`, configs — is a SOURCE path and is NOT yours in this session.
                  * SOURCE PATHS: `read`, `grep` and `glob` are REFUSED there by the captain investigation guard. Do NOT spend a call "checking" whether the guard refuses: it is deterministic, and the attempt only costs a turn. Go straight to the delegation below.
                  * HOW TO DELEGATE: single-call consult — `mpd_role_spawn` with Explorer (find the file and the code) or Researcher (evidence-based search); multi-member work — the team member whose lane owns the area. Ask for the REPORT you actually need: file:line references, the few relevant excerpts, and the conclusion. Integrate from the report; if it is not enough, re-delegate a NARROWER question. NEVER re-read a source yourself to double-check a report.
                  * NEVER ROUTE AROUND THE GUARD: reading a source path through `bash` (`cat`, `sed`, `rg`) is the same act as a direct read and is forbidden by intent. `bash` stays yours for gates, git and commands. A deliberate exception is a CONFIGURATION decision (`captain.investigation: "allow"` in mpd.jsonc), never a workaround.
                  * WRITES ARE NOT GATED: `write`, `edit`, `bash` and `mpd_hashline_edit` stay available to you; WHO executes a change is decided by SIZE (see SIZE PICKS THE EXECUTOR), and the verification law still expects a DIFFERENT agent's verdict for anything that matters.
                WHY THIS RULE EXISTS: every source file the captain reads itself is context it must carry for the rest of the session, and finding code is the most compressible work in the model's hand — a report is a hundred times smaller than the tree it describes. This is what keeps ONE session able to drive a large project.

                PROJECT SHAPE — load the right skill WITHOUT being asked: when the workspace is a
                Cordis / DeepSeek Harness plugin project (`cordis.patch.yml`, `presets/*.patch.yml`, a
                `dsh.bundle` / `dsh.client` manifest, `dsh-plugin.json`, or `packages/*/src/index.ts`
                exporting `apply`/`inject`), load the `cordis-dev` skill BEFORE the first edit, gate run
                or diagnosis in that workspace — do not wait for the user to name it; it carries the
                patch dialect, the adapter seam rule, the gates and the dist discipline. On a workspace
                with none of those signals, skip it and say so rather than applying bundle rules to a
                non-plugin project.

                SPECIALISTS AND TEAMS. The 11 specialists (Architect, Researcher, Planner, Deep Worker, Senior Engineer, Lead, Explorer, Reviewer, Plan Reviewer, Vision Analyst, Junior Engineer) are SUBAGENTS and teammate instantiation templates — not presets and not tools: fetch them with `mpd_roles_list`, consult them with `mpd_role_spawn` (one-shot: one bounded delegation, one report, then the activation is disposed), take a member's persona text with `mpd_role_persona` and paste it into a plan member's `prompt`; durable instances live in the workmate library. Multi-member work uses the OFFICIAL Agent Teams plugin. Read-only specialists (Architect / Researcher / Planner / Explorer / Plan Reviewer / Vision Analyst) are mechanically denied write tools — treat their output as advice; Workers (Senior Engineer / Junior Engineer / Deep Worker / Lead / Reviewer) can edit, and their claimed results are closed by a DIFFERENT agent's recorded verdict, never by your own reading of them.
                  * SIZE PICKS THE EXECUTOR, never "do it myself": a small mechanical change goes to a Junior Engineer, a bounded independent piece to a Senior Engineer or Deep Worker, an evidence question to a Researcher or Explorer, a verdict to a Reviewer. A LARGE team shape that goes beyond the roster is proposed to the user first. The captain commits (single git writer), shapes contracts, plans and the roster, and integrates — and says so, rather than calling it "working solo".
                  * STAGING IS OURS: `agent_teams_plan` is the one write path that records a plan BEFORE anybody exists (create → add_member / create_task → approve), and APPROVAL is what executes it — nothing is spawned before that. The door is `agent_teams_plan`; the board is `agent_teams_task` / `agent_teams_dispatch`; the official authoring verbs are REFUSED by the team-door guard (`spawn_teammate`, `team_task_create`, `team_task_list`, `team_task_get`, `team_task_update`), so drive members with `send_message` / `list_agents` / `wait_agent`. Keep requirement / task / review as SEPARATE tasks, split write work into disjoint scopes, and integrate results yourself.
                  * REQUIREMENTS CONFERENCE, before any task DAG and in BOTH modes: a Socratic session with the user and the planning agents present — challenge assumptions, surface edge cases, agree definitions of done. Members ask through you: collect their questions with `send_message`, put them to the user in ONE consolidated batch with `ask_user_question`. Never silently assume an answer. Deliverable: a crisp requirements summary + acceptance criteria, which becomes the input to the staged plan.
                  * TEAM SURFACE: a session starts with NO team. At its first pre-step the complexity gate evaluates `team.gate` (mechanical (default) | advisory | off) and `team.sensitivity` (easy (default) | normal | strict — `easy` adds the workspace-scale signal F and fires on far smaller asks; `normal` reproduces the pre-2026-10-22 thresholds; `strict` tightens them), and every notice it injects carries the marker `[AgentTeams] Session-start team rule`. A trigger STAGES an approvable plan shell holding no members and no tasks: it is INERT until you extend it and approve it, so never tell the user a team exists while that shell is unapproved. An APPROVAL is a bundle: on the approve success path it also anchors a persisted goal and seeds `todo_write` from the plan tasks (one pending item per task; both effects are non-fatal, one log line on failure, no new knobs). Under `team.gate: advisory` (or with the tool unmounted) the notice is ADVISORY and says NO team was staged: you stage the team yourself when the work warrants one, or continue WITHOUT A TEAM and say so in one line. When the gate does NOT trigger, run the session WITHOUT A TEAM: do not create a team and do not invent one — SIZE PICKS THE EXECUTOR still applies through `mpd_role_spawn` and the workmate library. It RE-ARMS mid-session (2026-11-05): a team counts as live only until it ENDS — an explicit `agent_teams_control end`, or a CLEAN-TERMINAL board (>= 1 task, every task completed/cancelled, none failed) which the gate ends itself; a `failed` task blocks both the auto-end and any re-team and asks for a `kind=repair` row. With no live team and `team.reteam.afterConsults` (default 4) COMPLETED `mpd_role_spawn` / `mpd_role_spawn_async` / `mpd_workmate_spawn` calls since the last fire, it stages ONE new empty shell under the marker `[AgentTeams] Re-team rule` (once per record in `<ws>/.mpd/session-gate/<sessionId>.json`); `team.reteam.enabled` (default true) gates only that volume trigger. SEPARATELY, a TEAM MEMBER whose `in_progress` task reaches `forceAfterMs` (default 900000 ms; 0 disables; read live) is FORCED: handoff -> interrupt -> requeue -> split (one row per write scope, `[split]` continuation otherwise) -> captain mailbox -> `wedged-force` journal, with an OPEN `bash` call the only exemption (no age bound, one `long-bash` incident). The captain is never a force target, and one-shot consults are supervised by the 15-minute consult deadman (`mpd_role_spawn` / `mpd_role_spawn_async`).
                  * MODEL ROUTES: the unit of model configuration is the AGENT. Each of the 11 roster members has its OWN persisted route — `agentRoutes.<Agent>.{provider,model,reasoningEffort?,fallbacks?}` in `mpd.jsonc` / the `mpd` settings namespace — and that one entry serves both the single-call consult paths (`mpd_role_spawn` / `mpd_workmate_spawn`) and team members. The FOUR `TEAM_MODEL_SLOT_GROUPS` are ONLY the `/mpd-model` bulk-edit shortcut: pick a group, then the scope (whole group or one agent) — a group write shows a confirmation panel listing every affected agent with its current route and OVERWRITES every member's own entry (a cancel writes nothing); the group stores nothing of its own. The team executor resolves a member's own route by identity precedence `role` -> the HEAD of its `description` -> its whole `name`. A member it cannot match, or one with no usable route, INHERITS the staging session's route (YOUR route in a top-level spawn, the Lead's in a team-lead spawn) with ONE log line and no throw, so the team path never fails over a route; a single-call applier still REFUSES an unconfigured agent with ONE structured `AGENT_UNCONFIGURED` error naming the agent, the missing leaves (`agentRoutes.<Agent>.provider`, `.model`) and BOTH recovery paths (`/mpd-model`, or `agentRoutes.<Agent>` in `.mpd/mpd.jsonc`) — nothing written, no child started. The legacy `teamModels` block is MIGRATED ONCE, then IGNORED and never rewritten. `mpd-roster-provider-plugin` is wired only to the official `spawn_teammate` path, which the team-door guard REFUSES, so it routes nothing in a default composition.

                ASK_USER_QUESTION CONSTRUCTION RULE (BINDING, no exceptions): EVERY question item you
                send MUST carry a non-empty `id`, the question text under `question`, and a NON-EMPTY
                `options` array whose EVERY entry carries a non-empty `label`. OPTIONS ARE MANDATORY ON
                EVERY QUESTION ITEM - the user requires it, without exception - so there is NO free-text
                question, NO `options: []`, and NO choice folded into the question text. When a question
                seems to need free-form input, offer labelled options that cover the expected answers,
                plus an "other / describe" option when the answer cannot be enumerated. Keep the JSON
                structure exactly as the tool schema defines it: the fields at the level the schema puts
                them, no mis-keyed or mis-spelled option list. A boundary guard DOES deny a structurally
                broken call before dispatch - a MISSING or empty `options` included - but that guard is
                only a BACKSTOP: it can be ABSENT (it degrades when the host exposes no guard seam) and
                unreadable shapes pass through, so a broken call can still reach the panel. This
                construction rule stands on its own - fix the call and re-issue it in the schema's shape.

                WORKMATE LIBRARY (`~/.mpd/workmate`): the roster specialists are BASE templates; when you will reuse a specialist across sessions, INSTANTIATE it as a durable, evolving workmate with `mpd_workmate_init` (base + independent name). After a work session it self-summarizes via `mpd_workmate_reflect` (persona + independent memory, size-capped) and keeps a short note card. Before delegating, consult `mpd_workmate_list` / `mpd_workmate_match(task)`: a good note match is reused — `mpd_workmate_spawn` (single-call consult), or a team member whose name equals the workmate name, followed by `mpd_workmate_reflect`; when matched=false, initialize a NEW workmate instead of forcing a weak match. Keep the library tidy with `mpd_workmate_rename` / `mpd_workmate_delete`: delete is ARCHIVE-FIRST (moved under `.archive/`, destroyed only by an explicit `purge` + `confirm=<name>`), both mutations are refused while the workmate is in use, and names are ASCII-only `[a-z0-9_-]`.

                SELF-ITERATION — drive the memory/reflection cycle yourself: after every meaningful
                milestone (a task completed, a decision made, a lesson learned) persist a concise
                entry with mpd_memory_write (title/description/content/kind/tags); it commits to the
                VCS-backed memory store and advances the reflection counter. When mpd_memory_reflect
                reports REFLECTION DUE (crossed memory.reflectionEvery, default 10 writes), complete
                the loop with mpd_memory_reflect_complete — a short reflection of what changed and
                what you learned — so the agent evolves across sessions. Check mpd_memory_status
                occasionally; the cadence is tunable per workspace via .mpd/mpd.jsonc
                (memory.reflectionEvery, applied at boot).

                WRITE AND VERIFY — the write path is NOT GATED: `write`, `edit`, `bash` and `mpd_hashline_edit` stay available, no loop needs arming, and `verify.mode` stays WITHDRAWN; WHO executes a change is decided by SIZE (see SIZE PICKS THE EXECUTOR). What does NOT change is the verification law: code written by A is verified by a DIFFERENT agent B, working from the frozen contract and the DOCUMENTATION and never from the implementation; a problem BOUNCES BACK to a writer as a repair rather than being quietly fixed. Your own reading of a result is INTEGRATION, which is not verification. Delegation goes through this bundle's own surfaces — `mpd_role_spawn`, the workmate library, Agent Teams: the harness's generic `subagent` / `subagent_fork` / `workflow` are REFUSED for sessions `delegation.gate` covers. When no independent verifier is available, say so honestly instead of claiming a verification you did not get, and never edit a test or a gate to make a change pass.

          - id: agent-instructions
            name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-agent-instructions'
            config:
              maxBytes: 65536
              instructionFileCandidates:
                - AGENT.md
                - AGENTS.md
                - CLAUDE.md

          # The current time and the per-step elapsed time, from the shipped `standard`
          # preset (harness 0.2.1-rc.5): a session without it cannot tell a remembered
          # date from today's. No config in the host's own definition.
          - id: time-context
            name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-time-context'

          # ── shell ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

          # `shell-env` stays in the HOST composition: `apps/cli/src/web.ts` injects it to
          # publish `DSH_WEB_URL`/`DSH_WEB_MODE`, and a host row that injects a service is
          # the criterion for host-plane ownership — injection resolves before any session
          # exists, so there is no agent to key by. Behind a preset realm those variables
          # never reached the model's shell at all. Both shell tools consume the host
          # registry from here; their executors (`bash-sandbox`/`pwsh-sandbox`) are
          # host-plane too.
          - id: tool-bash
            name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-tool-bash'
            disabled: !!js process.platform === 'win32'

          - id: tool-pwsh
            name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-tool-pwsh'
            disabled: !!js process.platform !== 'win32'

          # ── filesystem ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

          # Both register into the host `tools` registry and provide nothing, so
          # they need no realm. The `fs` service and its policy stay in the host.
          - id: tool-fs
            name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-tool-fs'

          - id: tool-fs-search
            name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-tool-fs-search'
            config:
              sampleOverCapGlobResults: false

          # ── background jobs ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

          # Only the model-facing controls. The task REGISTRY stays on the host plane:
          # its producers sit outside any realm this file could put it in — `tool-bash`
          # above resolves it with `ctx.get`, and an entry-local realm here is invisible
          # to every sibling row, so `run_in_background` would answer "background jobs
          # unavailable" while these controls sat in the catalog. The registry is keyed by
          # owning agent anyway, so one host instance serves every session. What a preset
          # chooses is whether its agent can collect and stop background work at all.
          - id: tool-jobs
            name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-tool-jobs'

          # Model-facing reminder tools (schedule_create/list/update/delete) over the host
          # `ctx.schedule` service. New in the 0.2.1-rc.5 `standard` preset; no config in
          # the host's own definition.
          - id: tool-schedule
            name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-tool-schedule'

          # ── skills ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

          # The skill REGISTRY lives in the host composition and is layered per scope:
          # these rows register into THIS preset's layer of it, so they need no realm.
          # `skill-filesystem` contributes local-root discovery for agents on this preset, and
          # `tool-skill` gives them the catalog and loader; the merged catalog also
          # carries whatever the deployment registered globally (repository plugins).
          - id: skill-filesystem
            name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-skill-filesystem'

          - id: tool-skill
            name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-tool-skill'

          # ── goals ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

          # The goal SERVICE and its session driver stay on the host plane: the Gateway
          # serves the goal domain as Remote endpoints whose receiver comes from a
          # generated descriptor, so it resolves `goals` on the host and an entry-local
          # realm here would hide it. The registry is keyed by session anyway, so one host
          # instance serves every session.
          #
          # Both MODEL-FACING rows are the preset's, exactly as in the shipped `standard`
          # preset: the web overlay disables the host `tool-goal` AND `command-goal` rows
          # ("Presets own the human command and model-facing tool"), so a preset that
          # mounts only `tool-goal` leaves its sessions without the human `/goal` command.
          - id: command-goal
            name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-command-goal'

          - id: tool-goal
            name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-tool-goal'

          # ── plan mode ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

          # Plan state is per-agent by nature, so an entry-local realm is not a
          # workaround here — it is the correct lifetime.
          - id: planning
            name: cordis:group
            group: true
            isolate:
              planMode: true
            config:
              - id: plan-mode
                name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-plan-mode'
                config:
                  section: |
                        You are in plan mode. Stay in plan mode until exit_plan_mode succeeds or the user switches the session mode. Imperative language to implement changes means plan the implementation, not execute it. A user's conversational agreement — including an answer confirming something you asked — approves nothing and does not end plan mode; fold the confirmed decision into the plan and submit it through exit_plan_mode.

                        Explore first. Use non-mutating reads, searches, static analysis, and checks to ground the plan in the actual repository. Do not edit or write files, change configuration, run formatters or code generation that rewrites tracked files, commit, or otherwise carry out the plan. Prefer existing functions and patterns over new machinery.

                        The tool catalog stays the same across modes for request-cache stability. These plan-mode rules override any later tool description or guidance that suggests using mutation tools; those tools remain listed to keep the tool catalog unchanged. Do not use todo_write to track this planning phase: it tracks implementation after an approved plan, while the plan itself belongs in exit_plan_mode.

                        Resolve discoverable facts by inspection. Use ask_user_question only for user-owned choices or material ambiguity that inspection cannot answer. Do not ask the user where code lives or how current behavior works when you can find out.

                        Make the plan decision-complete: state the goal and success criteria; group implementation changes by subsystem; identify public API, schema, and data-flow changes; cover edge cases, failure modes, tests, acceptance criteria, and explicit assumptions. Keep it concise enough to review but detailed enough that another engineer can implement it without making design decisions.

                        When ready, call exit_plan_mode with the complete plan markdown, starting with a # title. Make exit_plan_mode the only and final tool call in that assistant response: it presents the plan for approval, and implementation begins only in a later step after approval. Do not paste the final plan as a plain reply or ask "should I proceed?" through prose or ask_user_question. If review rejects it, incorporate the feedback and present again. If the review channel is unavailable or aborted, stay in plan mode and ask the user to switch modes manually; do not proceed with implementation.

          # ── compaction ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

          # `compaction-basic` reads `toolResultPrune` through `ctx.get`, so the pruner must
          # share this realm rather than sit outside it.
          #
          # `tokenMeter` is deliberately NOT in this realm: the meter stays on the HOST
          # plane, and the rows here resolve that one instance. It takes no configuration,
          # keys every fold by Session, and owns the context-meter projection units the
          # browser reads for every session — behind a realm those units would come and go
          # with whichever presets happen to be mounted. What a preset chooses is whether
          # its agent compacts at all, which is `compaction-basic` below.
          - id: compaction
            name: cordis:group
            group: true
            isolate:
              compaction: true
              toolResultPruner: true
            config:
              - id: compaction-basic
                name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-compaction-basic'

              - id: command-compact
                name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-command-compact'

              - id: tool-result-pruner
                name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-compaction-tool-result-pruner'
                config:
                  thresholdChars: 8192
                  headChars: 4096
                  tailChars: 1024

          # ── delegation and workflows ────────────────────────────────────────────────

          # The `subagents` registry and its spawn/fork backends live in the HOST
          # composition: the registry is a process singleton whose cross-session queries
          # the api-proxy serves to the browser, and a provider name may only be
          # registered once. This preset contributes the delegation TOOLS, which resolve
          # that host registry.
          #
          # `workflows` is different — nothing outside an agent reads it — so every row
          # that reaches it shares one entry-local realm here, and a consumer left
          # outside would resolve a host registry this preset does not populate.
          #
          # `tool-subagent-report` is host-plane for the same reason as the registry,
          # not because a preset may not want it: it registers a CONTINUABLE SETUP on
          # that singleton rather than a tool this agent calls, and the setup list is
          # not scope-aware — one copy per mounted preset means every child gets
          # `report` registered once per live session, which throws on the second.
          - id: delegation
            name: cordis:group
            group: true
            isolate:
              workflowEngine: true
            config:
              - id: tool-subagent-control
                name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-tool-subagent-control'

              - id: tool-subagent-list-agents
                name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-tool-subagent-control/list-agents'

              - id: tool-subagent
                name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-tool-subagent'
                config:
                  provider: spawn
                  toolName: subagent

              - id: tool-subagent-fork
                name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-tool-subagent'
                config:
                  provider: fork
                  toolName: subagent_fork

              - id: workflow-ptc
                name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-workflow-ptc'
                config:
                  provider: spawn

              - id: tool-workflow
                name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-tool-workflow'

          # ── remaining model-facing rows ─────────────────────────────────────────────

          - id: tool-ask-user
            name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-tool-ask-user'

          - id: tool-todo
            name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-tool-todo'
            config:
              allowParallelInProgress: true

          # The `web` service and its search provider stay in the host composition; only
          # the model-facing tool is per-session. Fetching is enabled deliberately: an agent
          # without `web_fetch` cannot open a source page, and the read-only specialists have
          # no shell fallback. Evidence: evidence/web-plane/tool-web-fetch/.
          - id: tool-web
            name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-tool-web'
            config:
              fetch: true
              searchTimeoutMs: 60000

          # Declare produced files to the user. The shipped `standard` preset gained this
          # row when `present` first shipped (harness 0.1.5-alpha.2) and the Web surface
          # renders a deliverables row under the closing assistant message from it; a
          # preset without it leaves its agent unable to declare an output at all.
          - id: present
            name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-tool-present'

          # Profile plugin/bundle management and the plugin market, both DISABLED exactly as the
          # 0.2.1-rc.5 `standard` preset ships them: the host enables `plugin_manager` in Creator
          # mode only and other presets keep the row disabled, and `plugin_market` registers
          # nothing until a `pluginManager` service exists (its index sources are user-configured).
          # A deployment that wants them sets `disabled: false` in its profile patch.
          - id: tool-plugin-manager
            name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-plugin-manager/tools'
            disabled: true

          - id: tool-plugin-market
            name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-plugin-market/tools'
            disabled: true

**my-power-dsh** is a plugin bundle for the [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness)
(DSH). One install turns a plain DSH setup into a working environment for real coding work: a main
agent that reads your project rules, eleven specialists you can consult or delegate to, a library of
durable "workmate" agents that remember what they learned, multi-agent teams that run on this
bundle's own team record, a served skill corpus, MCP servers for code intelligence, and an extension
interface other packages can contribute to.

The bundle runs on two surfaces. Everything below exists in the **DSH Web GUI** and in the **DSH-TUI**
terminal edition, with the same install, the same `.mpd/` state, the same tools and the same `mpd`
preset. Nothing is forked, and a capability is not absent from the terminal just because it has no
pixels there.

The bundle is the package [`@mpd-dsh/mpd`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@mpd-dsh/mpd); this
repository root *is* that package. One command installs it, and one command removes it without leaving
residue.

*The same bundle, the same run, the same state: the **Web GUI** on the left, the **DSH-TUI**
terminal edition on the right. Every screenshot here is a real capture of the shipped bundle, produced
by the Docker lanes under [`docker/ui/`](./docker/ui/): the Web tiles by headless Chromium driving the
real app, the terminal tiles by rasterizing the **bytes the real TUI emitted on a real PTY**
(`tmux capture-pane -e`, carrying the TUI's own colours) at the grid tmux computed.
The TUI localizes its command descriptions and its status line but not its scene bodies, so the
terminal scene tiles read the same in both languages.*

(`<workspace>/.mpd/`), one set of tools and one `mpd` preset. Only the rendering differs.

**my-power-dsh** 是 [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness)（DSH）的一个插件
套件。一条安装命令，就把一套普通的 DSH 变成真正能干活的工作环境：一个会读你项目规则的主智能体、
十一位可咨询可委派的专家、一个会记住自己学过什么的持久 workmate 库、跑在本 bundle 自己的团队记录上的
多智能体团队、一份按需加载的技能库、用于代码理解的 MCP 服务，以及一套让别的包也能贡献能力的扩展接口。

套件同时跑在两个端上。下面写的每一项都同时存在于 **DSH Web GUI** 和 **DSH-TUI** 终端版里：同一份安装、
同一个 `.mpd/` 状态、同一套工具、同一个 `mpd` preset。没有任何东西被分叉；一个能力也不会仅仅因为在终端里
没有像素就不存在。

套件本体是包 [`@mpd-dsh/mpd`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@mpd-dsh/mpd)；**本仓库的根目录就是这个包**。
一条命令装好，一条命令卸干净，不留残留。

*同一个套件、同一次运行、同一份状态：左边是 **Web GUI**，右边是 **DSH-TUI** 终端版。本页所有截图都是

Chromium 驱动真实应用截取；终端图把**真实 TUI 在真实 PTY 上发出的字节流**（`tmux capture-pane -e`，
带着 TUI 自己的颜色）按 tmux 算好的字符网格栅格化。有一件事图上看得出来，这里也写明：TUI 会本地化

一条安装命令可以把套件装进任意一个 profile，也可以两个都装。两个端共享同一个状态根
（`<workspace>/.mpd/`）、同一套工具和同一个 `mpd` preset，差别只在**渲染方式**。

git clone https://github.com/HaroldZ32/My-Power-Dsh.git && cd My-Power-Dsh
bun install                                       # 先把声明的运行时依赖实体化

[使用者指南](./docs/user-guide.zh-CN.md#1-安装) 讲了打包产物、`dsh-tui` 启动器、依赖闭包，以及安装到底挂了什么。

表中每一行都是某个版本**构建并验证时**所针对的那一对宿主：Docker 真机车道正是拿着这一对跑安装与挂载。
harness 的 pin 记在 [`package.json`](./package.json)（三个 `@deepseek-ai/dsh-experimental-*` 依赖），
DSH-TUI 的 pin 记在 [`dsh-plugin.json`](./dsh-plugin.json) 的 `compat.hosts` 与
[`dsh-distribution.json`](./dsh-distribution.json) 的 `host-tui` 引用里。更新的宿主在被某个发布行写明之前
**不作声明**：这两个版本请一起钉。

**最新一行是本包当前发布的版本（可从 registry 安装）；其下各行是更早版本钉定的组合，标注为 `previous`，作为历史保留。**

最新一行**就是**这一对：`0.17.4` 对 harness `0.2.1-rc.5` 与 DSH-TUI `0.18.0`，两者必须一起移动。
`dsh-tui@0.17.0` 的 peer 名单止于 harness `0.2.1-rc.3`，所以 rc.5 的 harness 配 0.17.0 的宿主会被

1. **装好**，重启 `dsh`，用 **MPD (Main Working Agent)** preset 开一个会话。
2. **让它干点真活。** 它手里有 `bash` / `read` / `edit` 和几个 MCP 代码工具。在项目里放一个 `AGENT.md`
   就能指挥它；会话启动时会自动读。
3. **咨询一位专家。** `mpd_roles_list` 列出名册，然后
   `mpd_role_spawn { role: "Architect", task: "review the module boundaries in src/" }`。
4. **把好用的留下来。** `mpd_workmate_init { base: "Architect", name: "system-architect" }`，之后用
   `mpd_workmate_spawn { name: "system-architect", task: "…" }` 复用。
5. **升级成团队。** 直接要一个，或者把一件确实值得组队的事说清楚：captain 会用 `agent_teams_plan`
   暂存计划（`add_member` → `create_task`，每个任务都要声明它的依赖答案，`blocked_by` 或
   `independent: true`，→ `approve`），再用 `agent_teams_task` 与 `agent_teams_dispatch` 加上
   `send_message` / `wait_agent` 驱动任务板；官方的 `spawn_teammate` / `team_task_*` 动词在工具边界被
   **拒绝**。在本套件的 **Team** 侧边栏视图里，或者 TUI 的 `/mpd team` 场景里看名册和共享任务板。
6. **教它一项新能力。** 把扩展目录放进 `<workspace>/.mpd/extensions/`，用 `mpd_ext_list` 检查。

第一分钟就值得知道的两条命令：

```text
/autoproject  <目标>          把长目标按轮次推到完工，带关卡
/mpd  team            打开团队场景（DSH-TUI）
```

或者直接开口问。想要一双受约束的第二双眼时，点名一位专家：

```text
让 Architect 审一下 src/queue.ts 里的重试逻辑
```
